scoring_checks: The four one-point criteria cover first-order support, the exact trial-step coefficient, both endpoint contributions plus the zero modulus, and the final global norm bound. Their mathematics and the reference proof are correct. Criterion 2 explicitly allows equivalent descent estimates; criterion 3 already allows any valid argument at β=0.

Criteria 1 and 4 read as mandatory proof implementations. The first can deny credit to the very same-z two-model proof in the cited Lean, which proves the affine-tilt calculation without introducing F_x or separately stating its minimization. The fourth can deny credit to a cancellation-free solution: for n=‖d‖ and r=β‖y−x‖, derive n²≤nr≤(n²+r²)/2 by Young's inequality, then take nonnegative square roots. Correct equivalent proofs need explicit full-credit treatment, not just variants of the zero case.

Part (3.5) uses real β with 0≤β, and LipschitzWith uses β:NNReal with no strict positivity requirement. Affine functions, even a constant objective if an optimizer is required, show why smoothness does not force positivity.

The source problem ranges over Euclidean ℝᵈ and the owned declarations range over complete real inner-product spaces on Set.univ. Finite-dimensional Euclidean space specializes the Lean domain; completeness in the generalization supports the genuine Riesz gradient. Nothing in the proof licenses moving the trial point outside a constrained domain.

exercise_semantic_slots.objects: A real-valued convex C¹ objective f, its genuine gradient, x and y, D_f(y,x), d=∇f(y)−∇f(x), and the affine tilt F_x with its descent trial point.
exercise_semantic_slots.domains: All of Euclidean ℝᵈ in the source; all of a complete real inner-product space in Lean. β is nonnegative in the upper model, strictly positive only where the reciprocal is used.
exercise_semantic_slots.quantifiers: The upper model holds for all ordered pairs a,b. For every x the tilt is minimized at x against every z. All three conclusions apply to every x,y in their stated modulus domains, and the limiting argument fixes the pair before ε tends to zero.
exercise_semantic_slots.assumptions: Global C¹, convexity and the global quadratic upper model with β≥0; β>0 for (3.4). No gradient-Lipschitz, optimizer, Hessian, nonzero d, or positive dimension is needed in the argument.
exercise_semantic_slots.conclusion: D_f(y,x)≥‖d‖²/(2β) for β>0, then ‖d‖²≤β⟨d,y−x⟩ and ‖d‖≤β‖y−x‖ for β≥0; in particular the gradient is constant at zero modulus.
exercise_semantic_slots.senses: Smoothness means (1.7), not the Lipschitz conclusion. Minimization is of the tilt, not of f. The scaled one-sided result is equivalent to the reciprocal only on β>0. The named Lean declarations are owned answers, not a distinct aligned Lean task.
exercise_semantic_slots.constants: Quadratic upper-model coefficient β/2, descent step length 1/β, Bregman lower coefficient 1/(2β), scaled one-sided multiplier 2β, and cocoercivity and Lipschitz multipliers β. Symmetrization uses two equal norm-square contributions.
